summary: Remove duplicates with a set, sort from biggest to smallest, and take the second item if it exists. "Second highest DISTINCT" means repeats of the top score don't count.

blocks.title: Read the scores
blocks.text: N on one line, the scores on the next, as `int`s (they may be negative).

blocks.title: Distinct scores, biggest first
blocks.text: `set(scores)` drops repeats, so `90 85 90` becomes `{90, 85}`. `sorted(…, reverse=True)` lists them from highest to lowest. Without the set, the second item could just be another 90.

blocks.title: Not enough different scores
blocks.text: If everyone has the same score (or N = 1), there is no second highest, so we print `Second highest: None`. Reading `distinct[1]` here would crash.

blocks.title: Print the second item
blocks.text: Index 1 is the second highest distinct score.

complexity: Time O(N log N) for the sort with N ≤ 1000 — instant.
pitfalls: Forgetting the set → a repeated top score is reported as second.
No check for fewer than 2 distinct scores → `IndexError`.
